summary: Jim Taylor works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Macquarie University by 1989 and served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide, attested in 2014.

Jin Y. Park specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held a post as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and was a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

Jinah Kim is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at UC Berkeley. She has held posts at Harvard University, Vanderbilt University, and the Institute for Advanced Study as a Mellon fellow (2009–2010).

Jinbo Shi is a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Minzu University of China and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. His career includes posts at CASS from 1975 and Minzu University around 2002.
Jinchuan Wan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 2010, he is attested as a professor at both National Central University and Fo Guang University.
Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He served as a Director at the University of Hong Kong, attested between 2006 and 2010.

Jing-shen Tao specializes in sinology and history and archaeology. After earning his Ph.D. from Indiana University (~1963–1967), he served as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–1999) and Correspondence Research Fellow at Academia Sinica (~1990).
Jingru Wang was a scholar in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1927–1930) and held a post at Minzu University of China (~1952–1958).

Jinhua Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology, with studies at McMaster University and Kyoto University. He has held posts at the University of Virginia and the University of British Columbia, where he was professor of East Asian Buddhism (attested 2008–2018).

Jinhua Jia is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned her PhD at the University of Colorado. She held posts at the University of Colorado, Harvard University, City University of Hong Kong, and The Hong Kong Polytechnic University.
Jinling He is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Koki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2009.

Jinshi Fan works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1958–1963) under Su Bai, she served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014) and became a part-time professor at Lanzhou University (~2004).

Jinzhang Peng was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as deputy director in the Department of History at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) and later as a researcher and archeological institute dean at Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).
Jiro Abe was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907). He subsequently held academic posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).

Jiro Kawakita was a scholar of Tibetology who studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1943). He later held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1967–1977), the University of Tsukuba (~1978–1985), and Chubu University (~1985–1993).

Jiro Murata was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1920). He later held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College (~1962–1967).

Jiro Sugiyama was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies educated at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo National Museum (attested 1984–1986), Bukkyo University, Nagaoka University of Technology, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Jiryo Masuda was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Unrai Wogihara. He served as a professor at the University of Calcutta.
Jishu Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Rector at Choboji Monastery (attested 1914) and held a post as professor emeritus at Shuchiin University (attested 1977).
